result:
If I could change the world in one way, I’d make it dramatically easier for people to change their minds — not by forcing agreement, but by removing the social, cognitive, and algorithmic barriers that make open-mindedness punishing.

Many of the world’s hardest problems — polarization, misinformation, prejudice, stalled progress — are sustained less by bad people than by bad incentives: it costs us status, identity, and belonging to admit we were wrong. If we could update our beliefs without shame, we’d argue more honestly, trust more wisely, and solve more together.

In that world, curiosity would outweigh defensiveness, and truth would have a fighting chance.
